faqs.question: Is calling someone your garba partner romantic?
faqs.answer: It can be, but it does not have to be. In Hindi and Hinglish, गरबा पार्टनर covers both a dance companion and a date for the nine nights, so the person reads the tone from the rest of your message. If you want to keep it clearly friendly, गरबा साथी is the safer word.

faqs.question: What is the feminine form of saathi?
faqs.answer: साथिन (saathin) is the feminine form listed in the Hindi Shabdasagar. So to a woman you can write मेरी गरबा साथिन (meri garba saathin). The loanword पार्टनर has no feminine form; only the verb changes, बनोगी instead of बनोगे.

faqs.question: Can I call my best friend my jodidaar?
faqs.answer: You can, but it carries more weight than साथी. McGregor glosses जोड़ीदार as a mate or an equal, and its root जोड़ी means a pair, so it reads as a matched couple. For a best friend, गरबा साथी or the playful हमजोली fits better.

faqs.question: Why shouldn't I use saajhedaar for partner?
faqs.answer: साझेदार comes from साझा, which McGregor defines as partnership or a share in a company. It is the word for a business or property partner, so at garba it sounds like a contract. Use पार्टनर, साथी or जोड़ीदार instead.

faqs.question: Should I use tum or aap when asking?
faqs.answer: Use तुम (tum) for a friend, crush or spouse, and आप (aap) for someone you met recently or someone older. The verb follows the pronoun: बनोगे or बनोगी with तुम, बनेंगे with आप. तू (tu) is only for very close friends.

faqs.question: How do I type garba partner in Devanagari?
faqs.answer: It is written गरबा पार्टनर. On most phone keyboards you can switch to Hindi transliteration, type "garba partner" in Roman letters, and pick the Devanagari suggestion. If the person reads Hinglish more easily, sending the Roman spelling is perfectly normal.

faqs.question: Is hamjoli still used today?
faqs.answer: Yes, mostly for childhood friends. Bahri's dictionary gives "companion, playmate" with the example बचपन के हमजोली, childhood companions. It sounds nostalgic, so it suits an old friend rather than a new crush.

faqs.question: Do you actually need a partner to play garba?
faqs.answer: No. Garba itself is danced in a large circle, clapping in unison, so nobody keeps one fixed partner. A partner matters more in dandiya raas, where your sticks strike one person's at a time, and in the slang sense of who you go with.

faqs.question: Can I write my Be My Dandiya Partner invitation in Hindi?
faqs.answer: The page's interface is in English, but the nine lines and the note are free text you type yourself. Write them in Hindi or Hinglish, save to preview, and check they display correctly before you publish and send the link.

faqs.question: Does SubhSandesh help me find a garba partner?
faqs.answer: No. SubhSandesh does not match, rent or introduce people. The Be My Dandiya Partner page only helps you ask one person you already know, with nine lines, photos and a Yes/No they answer on their phone.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Garba Partner Meaning in Hindi: Which Word to Use and Why

The garba partner meaning in Hindi is simpler than it looks: most people just say गरबा पार्टनर (*garba partner*), keeping the English word. The Hindi-origin choices are गरबा साथी (*garba saathi*, companion), जोड़ीदार (*jodidaar*, a mate or one of a pair) and हमजोली (*hamjoli*, playmate), and each one says something different about the person you are asking.

There is roughly an even chance your word is read on a small screen: 48.3% of the pages shared through SubhSandesh are opened on a phone. It will often be typed in a hurry, too: in our nearest festival measurement, Raksha Bandhan 2026 (n=89, a different festival used here only as an analogue), 49.4% of pages were built on the festival day itself.

This page gives six Hindi words with their dictionary senses, a comparison table and ready-to-send lines in Devanagari and Hinglish. It also names the one word to avoid.

## What does "garba partner" mean in Hindi?

A garba partner (गरबा पार्टनर) is the person you go to garba with during Navratri, either a dance companion for the nine nights or, in the slang sense, a date. In Hindi the phrase carries both meanings at once, which is exactly why the word you choose matters.

The two senses come from how the dances work. UNESCO, which added Garba of Gujarat to its Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2023, describes dancers circling counter-clockwise while singing and clapping in unison. In that circle nobody keeps one partner, whereas in dandiya raas, the stick dance, your sticks meet one person's at a time.

So "मेरा गरबा पार्टनर" (*mera garba partner*) can mean a friend or a date. This page covers only the Hindi wording; the English sense of the phrase has its own explainer on this blog.

## 6 Hindi words for garba partner, and what each one signals

Each word gets the same four checks: sense, signal, grammar and recipient. Senses come from McGregor's *Oxford Hindi-English Dictionary*, Bahri's *Learners' Hindi-English Dictionary* and the Hindi Shabdasagar.

### 1. गरबा पार्टनर (garba partner)

- **Sense:** an English loanword. It has no entry in McGregor, Platts or Bahri, so no Hindi dictionary fixes its meaning.
- **Signals:** casual and deliberately vague; the reader decides if it means friend or date.
- **Grammar:** the noun does not change for gender, but the verb does: बनोगे (*banoge*) to a man, बनोगी (*banogi*) to a woman.
- **Send it to:** a crush, when you want the ask to feel light and leave room for a polite no.

### 2. गरबा साथी / साथिन (garba saathi / saathin)

- **Sense:** McGregor (p. 1004) glosses साथी as "companion; associate; ally". [Shabdasagar's entry](https://hi.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B8%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%A5%E0%A5%80) adds "one who stays with you" and "friend", and gives the feminine साथिन.
- **Signals:** warm and loyal, with no romantic pressure.
- **Grammar:** masculine साथी, feminine साथिन.
- **Send it to:** a best friend, a sibling or a cousin you dance with every year.

### 3. जोड़ीदार (jodidaar)

- **Sense:** McGregor lists it under [जोड़ी on p. 382](https://dsal.uchicago.edu/cgi-bin/app/mcgregor_query.py?qs=%E0%A4%9C%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%BC%E0%A5%80&searchhws=yes&matchtype=exact) as "a mate, partner, colleague; an equal".
- **Signals:** the matched pair, which is the dandiya sense, where your sticks meet one person's. It hints at a couple without saying "date".
- **Grammar:** a masculine noun ending in the Persian suffix -दार (*-daar*).
- **Send it to:** a spouse or steady partner, where "we are a pair" is already true.

### 4. हमजोली (hamjoli)

- **Sense:** Bahri (p. 692) gives "companion, playmate", with the example [बचपन के हमजोली](https://dsal.uchicago.edu/cgi-bin/app/bahri_query.py?qs=%E0%A4%B9%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%9C%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80&searchhws=yes&matchtype=exact), "childhood companions". Shabdasagar traces it to Persian हम (*ham*, same) plus Hindi जोड़ी.
- **Signals:** playful and nostalgic, with an old-film flavour.
- **Grammar:** a masculine noun.
- **Send it to:** a friend from your colony or school whom you have danced with since you were ten.

### 5. संगी (sangi)

- **Sense:** McGregor (p. 963) gives "an associate, friend" and, as an adjective, "devoted (to), fond (of)". Shabdasagar lists it as a synonym of साथी.
- **Signals:** literary and slightly formal; on its own it reads like poetry.
- **Grammar:** masculine; usually heard in the pair संगी-साथी (*sangi-saathi*, friends and companions).
- **Send it to:** a group caption rather than a one-to-one ask.

### 6. साझेदार (saajhedaar), the one to avoid

- **Sense:** McGregor (p. 1003) derives it from साझा, "partnership; association; share (in a company)".
- **Signals:** contracts and shops.
- **Grammar:** masculine.
- **Send it to:** nobody at garba.

## Hindi words for garba partner compared

The table leaves out संगी, which suits group captions rather than a one-to-one ask. पार्टनर is the safe default for ambiguity; जोड़ीदार quietly says "us".

| Word (Devanagari / Hinglish) | Dictionary sense, with source | Gender | Tone it sends |
|---|---|---|---|
| गरबा पार्टनर / garba partner | English loanword; not in McGregor, Platts or Bahri | Noun invariant; verb बनोगे/बनोगी | Casual, could be a date |
| गरबा साथी / garba saathi | "companion; associate; ally" (McGregor p. 1004) | m. साथी, f. साथिन | Warm, friendly |
| जोड़ीदार / jodidaar | "a mate, partner, colleague; an equal" (McGregor p. 382) | m. | Matched pair, couple-ish |
| हमजोली / hamjoli | "companion, playmate" (Bahri p. 692) | m. | Nostalgic, childhood friend |
| साझेदार / saajhedaar | from साझा, "partnership… share (in a company)" (McGregor p. 1003) | m. | Business; wrong at garba |

## Why most Hindi speakers just say "पार्टनर"

Most Hindi speakers keep the English word, and the research says this is normal rather than lazy. In a peer-reviewed study of Facebook comments, [Bali, Sharma, Choudhury and Vyas (2014)](https://aclanthology.org/W14-3914.pdf) analysed 40 posts and 6,983 comments from 22 to 28 October 2013. They found that 23.7% of the 398 Hindi sentences carried at least one English word, against 7.2% of English sentences carrying a Hindi one.

The paper also notes people choosing English nouns like "page" and "follower" even where a common Hindi equivalent exists. "Partner" behaves the same way.

The habit is growing. A 2024 open-access study in *Humanities and Social Sciences Communications* [found Hinglish use on Twitter rose 2% a year between 2014 and 2022](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41599-024-03058-6). The authors also found that mixing "affects the contextual meaning of different words differently", which is one reasonable reading of why पार्टनर, in festival Hinglish, now leans toward "date".

## How to ask someone to be your garba partner in Hindi

Two grammar choices change the tone more than the noun does: the pronoun and the verb ending. Use तुम (*tum*) for friends and partners and आप (*aap*) for someone you met recently or someone older. Then match the verb to the person, as in these five original lines, free to copy:

- **To a crush (female):** "इस नवरात्रि मेरी गरबा पार्टनर बनोगी?" (*Is Navratri meri garba partner banogi?*), meaning "Will you be my garba partner this Navratri?"
- **To a crush (male):** "नौ रातें, एक गोला, बस तुम्हारा जवाब बाकी है। मेरे गरबा पार्टनर बनोगे?" (*Nau raatein, ek gola, bas tumhara jawab baaki hai. Mere garba partner banoge?*), meaning "Nine nights, one circle, only your answer is left. Will you be my garba partner?"
- **To a best friend:** "हर साल की तरह इस बार भी मेरा गरबा साथी तू ही है।" (*Har saal ki tarah is baar bhi mera garba saathi tu hi hai.*), meaning "Like every year, you are my garba companion again."
- **To a spouse:** "डांडिया की हर ताल पर मुझे बस एक ही जोड़ीदार चाहिए।" (*Dandiya ki har taal par mujhe bas ek hi jodidaar chahiye.*), meaning "On every dandiya beat I want just one partner."
- **To someone you met recently:** "क्या आप इस शनिवार गरबा में मेरे पार्टनर बनेंगे?" (*Kya aap is Shanivaar garba mein mere partner banenge?*), meaning "Would you be my partner at garba this Saturday?"

The third line uses तू (*tu*), the most intimate "you". Between best friends it reads as affection; to a new acquaintance it reads as rude.

### Sending the ask as a page instead of a text

A WhatsApp line is enough for a friend. For a crush or a partner, SubhSandesh's [Be My Dandiya Partner invitation](https://subhsandesh.in/dandiya-partner) is built for that one-to-one question: you write nine short lines, one for each night, and add up to six photos and the date, time, venue and dress code. They open it in any phone browser with no app and no account: they light nine diyas, pick the colour they will twirl in, and answer.

The No button twirls away, and after five tries it turns into a second Yes. A yes ends in a 1080×1920 Dandiya Pass sized for an Instagram Story, and you get an email the first time they say yes.

**The page's buttons and interface are in English.** Your nine lines and note are free text, so write them in Hindi or Hinglish and use the preview to check they display correctly before publishing. You can also add a password: 38.5% of SubhSandesh creators lock their page before sharing it, which suits a question you would rather the group chat did not see.

## When a Hindi word or a link is the wrong choice

A link is the wrong tool for a group. The /dandiya-partner page asks one person one question, so it will not invite your society, your office or a home puja. Send those a plain message or a printed card, and if you want a different occasion page, [browse all SubhSandesh templates](https://subhsandesh.in/templates).

It is also wrong when the real question is bigger than garba. If what you mean is "come out with me", a page whose Yes turns into a countdown to a planned evening, such as [The Invitation for a date](https://subhsandesh.in/date-invitation), says that more honestly than calling someone a जोड़ीदार. SubhSandesh does not find, match or rent you a partner; it only helps you ask someone you already know.

Words misfire too: हमजोली to a new crush implies years of friendship you do not share. And if the person is standing next to you in the circle, just ask out loud. Our pages average 11.1 views each, but no reopening beats a face-to-face yes.

## Sources

- McGregor, *Oxford Hindi-English Dictionary* (DSAL): साथी p. 1004, [जोड़ी / जोड़ीदार p. 382](https://dsal.uchicago.edu/cgi-bin/app/mcgregor_query.py?qs=%E0%A4%9C%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%A1%E0%A4%BC%E0%A5%80&searchhws=yes&matchtype=exact), संगी p. 963, साझा p. 1003.
- Bahri, *Learners' Hindi-English Dictionary* (DSAL): [हमजोली, p. 692](https://dsal.uchicago.edu/cgi-bin/app/bahri_query.py?qs=%E0%A4%B9%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%9C%E0%A5%8B%E0%A4%B2%E0%A5%80&searchhws=yes&matchtype=exact).
- Hindi Shabdasagar, via Hindi Wiktionary: [साथी](https://hi.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B8%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%A5%E0%A5%80) (no publication date).
- Bali, Sharma, Choudhury, Vyas (2014). [“I am borrowing ya mixing?” An Analysis of English-Hindi Code Mixing in Facebook](https://aclanthology.org/W14-3914.pdf). ACL Workshop on Code Switching, 25 October 2014.
- Sengupta, Das, Akhtar, Chakraborty (2024). [Social, economic, and demographic factors drive the emergence of Hinglish code-mixing on social media](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41599-024-03058-6). *Humanities and Social Sciences Communications*, published 10 May 2024.

The table compares Hindi words, and nothing in content/facts.md (re-read in full 2026-10-12: product usage, reach, behaviour, festival lead time, miss-you segment) is per-word, per-language or about /dandiya-partner; no field records the language or script of a page's text. Inventing a column would be worse. Closes when the gifts DB is probed for Devanagari vs Roman text in /dandiya-partner line fields after Navratri 2026 and n reaches ~100 pages, giving a 'share of asks written in Devanagari' column.

auditReport.honestAssessment: An answer engine has a reason to cite this page: all 9 US-served results measured are off-intent and none names a Hindi word for partner, while this page gives six words with dictionary page numbers, gender and register, plus original Devanagari/Hinglish lines. The moat is that lexical work, not SubhSandesh data: the first-party facts concern delivery (phone opens, passwords, a Raksha Bandhan timing analogue) and no table column is first-party. India-served SERPs were not measured, the domain's authority is low, and a dictionary-literate competitor could copy the format quickly, so outcome is not predictable.
